newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS OPEN UP NINE POINT LEAD IN SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS OPEN UP NINE POINT LEAD IN SCOTLAND.

text.p: Ally McCoist extended his post-war Scottish League goalscoring record to 266 goals and helped stretch Rangers' lead at the top of the Scottish premier division before being carried off injured on Saturday.

McCoist struck after only five minutes in Rangers' 3-1 win over Dunfermline but Rangers needed late goals from Richard Gough and Danish substitute Erik Bo Andersen -- created by his compatriot Brian Laudrup -- to make sure of another victory in their quest to equal Celtic's Scottish record of nine successive championships.
Substitue Allan Moore scored a last-minute consolation for Dunfermline, who have now let in 14 goals against Rangers in three meetings this season.
Walter Smith's side are now nine points clear of second-placed Aberdeen and 11 clear of Celtic in the title race.
But Rangers ended the day without 17-goal McCoist, who appeared to twist his right knee after 74 minutes and had to be helped off.

Aberdeen, who beat Hearts 2-1 on Wednesday to move into second place above Celtic, stayed second but fell two points further behind Rangers when they were held to a 0-0 draw at home by lowly Motherwell.
Third placed Celtic did not play as their match with Raith was postponed because of international call-ups.
In the other games, Hibernian drew 1-1 with Dundee United and bottom-placed Kilmarnock scored a surprise 2-0 win over Hearts.
